target_customer: College students and local restaurants, later quick-service restaurants and local brands buying ordering, POS and creator marketing tools
problem: Students wanted fast pickup ordering and rewards for local food, while local restaurants lacked cheap digital ordering and loyalty tools.
business_model: Marketplace and restaurant software: monthly subscription plus sales commission from restaurants (per Yale Alumni Magazine 2018)
product_category: Food order-ahead app with social rewards

founders.name: Kevin Tan
founders.background_notes: Created the app during his senior year at Yale per Yale Alumni Magazine.

founders.name: Jamie Marshall
education: Yale University, class of 2019, neuroscience student (per TechCrunch and Yale Alumni Magazine)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Thiel Fellow and Forbes 30 Under 30.

founders.name: Jonathan Cameron
education: Ohio State University alumnus (per The Dartmouth)
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by Yale Alumni Magazine, TechCrunch and The Dartmouth; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile ordering app with payments and restaurant tablet integration, standard consumer app engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Social feed and campus density gave some network effects, but ordering apps were easy to copy and restaurants multihome.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Delivery incumbents offered pickup; Grubhub bought Tapingo in 2018 (per search summary, not opened). Snackpass later pivoted toward restaurant software and creator marketing.

market_need_then: By late 2017 Snackpass reported 7,000 users, over 60 New Haven restaurants and revenue from the start (Yale Alumni Magazine, Jan/Feb 2018).

branding.domain_note: Uses snackpass.co; trademark SNACKPASS filed November 2017 and registered June 2018 per a trademark aggregator.

identity.voice_and_tone: Casual and social; descriptions use emoji

branding.brand_signature: Social points and gifting of free food to friends
branding.community_and_virality: Company site claims 100 million social views; points can be exchanged for swag per a secondary analysis.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong campus word of mouth and social media presence, but no sourced press on the brand itself.

pivots.from: Consumer campus order-ahead and rewards app
pivots.to: Restaurant ordering, POS and creator marketing platform for local brands
pivots.why: Not stated in opened sources; homepage shows the current positioning

outcome_analysis: Snackpass grew from a Yale campus app to a company that raised a 21 million dollar Series A led by a16z in December 2019 and a 70 million dollar Series B in June 2021 at a reported valuation above 400 million dollars. It remains active but has shifted from consumer ordering toward restaurant software and creator marketing, and no later round was found.
notes: Series B valuation over 400 million per a Gunderson Dettmer note surfaced in search (not opened), so post_money left null. Series A reported as 21 million by TechCrunch; other trackers say 23.5 or 24 million. A January 2018 pre-seed seen only in one aggregator is unverified. Competitors: 2018 sources open (Yale Alumni Magazine) name none; Tapingo, Allset, Level Up, Ritual appear only in 2019 coverage so are not listed. Total raised about 91 million (sum of article figures, not stated).
